$comment: Figma assets whose code counterpart is NOT a top-level component, so no @figma JSDoc tag can point at them and scripts/check-figma-coverage.mjs would report them forever. Each entry is a deliberate statement that the asset IS mapped, just not the usual way. Keep this small: an entry is an admission that Figma and code model the same thing differently, and the better fix is usually to make them agree. Every entry needs a reason a reviewer can check.

overrides.name: CardProgress
overrides.reason: Compound member of Card. It IS a manifest entry, so an @figma tag would stick — but a compound part has no docs page of its own and should not need one. Overriding keeps the link honest without inventing a page.

overrides.name: CardMetric
overrides.reason: Compound member of Card. Same shape as CardProgress above.

overrides.name: TabTrigger
overrides.reason: Figma calls it TabTrigger, code calls it TabsTrigger — one letter apart, which is why no name match found it. It is a part of Tabs and has no docs page of its own, so it takes an override rather than a tag. Worth renaming one side to match; until then this records the pairing.

overrides.name: MenuItem
overrides.reason: Compound member of Menu (Radix DropdownMenu). Not exported on its own, so no JSDoc block can carry an @figma tag for it.

overrides.name: BreadcrumbItem
overrides.reason: Compound member. breadcrumb.tsx exports only Breadcrumb and crumbLabelVariants; the item is reached through the compound namespace.

overrides.name: PageButton
overrides.reason: Internal to Pagination — pagination.tsx exports only paginationRange and Pagination. Figma models the individual page button as a component because it needs the variants; code renders it inline.

overrides.name: TimelineItem
overrides.reason: A slot of Timeline (figma/disposition.json), so it takes an override rather than a tag. The Timeline component 2201:133 is built from its instances, and the item needs its own set for the tone and detail variants (redrawn from the hds#637 staging draft as 2252:127, replacing 2201:132).

overrides.name: NavListItem
overrides.reason: A compound part of NavList, mapped by override as TimelineItem is. The NavList component 2209:26 is built from its instances, and the item needs its own set for the Current and State variants.

overrides.name: SheetTrigger
overrides.reason: Compound member of Sheet (the element that opens the sheet). Code attaches the Radix Dialog part directly (Sheet.Trigger is a Radix Dialog part), so no JSDoc block can carry an @figma tag for it. The library draws it as a small component on the Sheet page next to the Sheet set 2265:119.

overrides.name: SheetTitle
overrides.reason: Compound member of Sheet (the heading that names the sheet). Code attaches the Radix Dialog part directly (Sheet.Title is a Radix Dialog part), so no JSDoc block can carry an @figma tag for it. The library draws it as a small component on the Sheet page next to the Sheet set 2265:119.

overrides.name: SheetDescription
overrides.reason: Compound member of Sheet (the supporting text). Code attaches the Radix Dialog part directly (Sheet.Description is a Radix Dialog part), so no JSDoc block can carry an @figma tag for it. The library draws it as a small component on the Sheet page next to the Sheet set 2265:119.

overrides.name: SheetClose
overrides.reason: Compound member of Sheet (the built-in close X). Code attaches the Radix Dialog part directly (Sheet.Close is a Radix Dialog part), so no JSDoc block can carry an @figma tag for it. The library draws it as a small component on the Sheet page next to the Sheet set 2265:119.

overrides.name: IconButton
overrides.reason: In code IconButton is <Button iconOnly>, one component; Figma draws it as its own set (owner decision 2026-11-05, hds#1147). check-figma-components holds the parity contract for it (figma/contracts/IconButton.json).
